thread:
Ava: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — wanted to capture the engineering process Q&A here for folks who couldn't make it. main topics: release cadence, oncall rotation, quality bars, and SLAs. TL;DR: leadership clarified quarterly-ish major releases + weekly patch cadence for infra/bug fixes. questions below.

Marcus: thanks Ava — yes that's the summary. Major releases every ~12 weeks with micro-releases/patches weekly; critical security fixes get expedited.

Sara: two quick clarifiers — what constitutes a "major" vs "minor" release? and is there a firm freeze window before majors?

Marcus: good q. major = schema/infra/model change that requires cross-team migrations or compatibility work. minor = feature flags, UX-only, small infra tweaks. freeze = 72 hours for majors (no non-critical merges).

Ravi: for Dedicated customers we heard SLA targets are 99.9% uptime and p95 latency target of 120ms for text gen — is that official? and how do we communicate degradations?

Marcus: yes, Dedicated baseline SLA: 99.9% for availability. Latency SLOs differ by model class; p95 120ms is the baseline for small context models on dedicated fleets — we'll publish a table in the SLA doc. Degradations: status page + customer alerts + support-runbook.

Jules: on quality bars — are we making unit test + integration test + eval suite pass gates mandatory for majors? what's the acceptance for model onboarding?

Ava: acceptance gates: automated unit + integration passing is required. For model changes we require an eval run on the canonical prompt set with no regressions > 2% F1 or qualitative review if the metric is fuzzy. Product sign-off required for customer-impacting behavior.

Priya: small operational ask — can we standardize the oncall rotation cadence? some teams use weekly, others use 2-week. I'd like a recommendation.

Sara: +1. Weekly is better for small teams to avoid fatigue over long term; 2-week works for larger pools. Recommendation: team lead chooses weekly or fortnightly, but keep primary+secondary overlap for handoffs. update runbooks accordingly.

Eve: a practical check — will we enforce branch protection for majors (no force pushes, required reviews, CI green)?

Ava: yes, branch protection will be enforced for major-release branches: 2 reviews, green CI, no force-push. We'll add a release checklist template.

Ravi: can someone drop the minimal pager/esc policy here? i.e., who to escalate to for infra vs model-misbehavior?

Priya: short version: Pager -> oncall primary (team) -> oncall secondary -> platform oncall (eng-sre) -> Marcus/lead oncall if P1. Model-misbehavior that impacts safety follows the safety escalation list first. I'll paste the snippet we use: 

```
Pager escalation: 
- P1: primary oncall -> secondary -> eng-sre -> exec oncall
- P2: primary -> secondary -> SRE followup during business hours
- Safety incident: notify Safety channel + Safety lead oncall immediately
```

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to infra-staging at 2026-06-02T02:30Z (runbook:test-release-check) :rocket:

Jules: does the rolling canary policy change for majors? earlier we had 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 hours.

Marcus: for majors we prefer a slower canary: 5% -> 20% (2h) -> 50% (4h) -> 100% (8h) with automated rollback on error budget breach or increased error rate > 1%. For minor patches the previous 10/50/100 pattern is fine.

Sara: action items from me: update runbook with freeze window text, add branch protection rules, and create a checklist PR template. I'll cc teams.

Ava: follow-ups: Marcus to publish SLA table, Priya to update escalation doc, Sara to submit PR for release checklist. I'll post the all-hands slide link here: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/2026-06-release-process-deck :eyes:

Marcus: thanks all. if anyone has specific edge-cases (e.g., model rollback during canary that still shows degraded but within error budget) DM me and we'll add to the playbook.

Ava: perfect — closing thread. I'll consolidate notes into the process doc and ping owners. :white_check_mark:
